finding.js_dependencies.risky_cdn: Script loaded from {host}, a compromised domain (2024 supply-chain attack): remove or replace it.
finding.js_dependencies.sri_missing: {count} third-party resource(s) without an integrity (SRI) attribute, including {scripts} script(s), from: {hosts}.
module.js_dependencies.checks: Detects the JavaScript libraries loaded by the page (CDNs and site files), their known vulnerabilities (OSV.dev and local table), subresource integrity (SRI) and compromised CDNs such as polyfill.io.
module.js_dependencies.fix:
If a script comes from `polyfill.io` or a domain run by the same operator (compromised in 2024), remove it immediately from your page templates, themes and tag managers: it can inject malicious code into your visitors' browsers. Replace it with a copy hosted by you or a trusted mirror loaded with `integrity`, and check that the site has not already redirected visitors.
Update each vulnerable library to the version given by "Fixed from" in the finding (or a newer one), then test the pages concerned.
If a library is no longer maintained (AngularJS for example), replace it with a maintained alternative; in the meantime, only pass trusted content through it.
Add the `integrity` and `crossorigin="anonymous"` attributes to every script and stylesheet loaded from another domain, with a pinned version in the address (never `latest`): the snippet shows the tag and the command that computes the hash.
Recompute the hash on every version change. If the browser blocks the resource, check the hash and the CDN's `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header.
Services whose content changes by design (Google Tag Manager, Stripe, Google fonts) cannot be protected by `integrity`: limit them with `script-src` in the `Content-Security-Policy`.
Better: host your libraries yourself (npm and a build, or a versioned copy) and track them with `npm audit` or a tool such as Dependabot or Renovate.
Run the scan again.
module.js_dependencies.fix_snippet:
# HTML
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib/1.2.3/lib.min.js"
  integrity="sha384-BASE64_HASH"
  crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

# Bash
curl -s https://cdn.example.com/lib/1.2.3/lib.min.js | openssl dgst -sha384 -binary | openssl base64 -A
module.js_dependencies.title: JavaScript dependencies
module.js_dependencies.why: An outdated library hands over a ready-made flaw, and a third-party script without SRI can be swapped for hostile code: a supply-chain attack.
